articles.title: Teens tell BBC of their hopes and fears as they prepare to start work
articles.summary: Follow four students from Newcastle as they try out roles for the first time as part of their work experience placements.
articles.body:
More than four in 10 UK teenagers want more work experience opportunities at school, with a similar proportion calling for more guidance on how to apply for jobs, a survey for the BBC suggests.

The online survey, by Survation , asked 2,000 young people aged 13 to 18 about the world of work and the help they need to secure employment once they leave full-time education.

As part of the Teen Summit project by Radio 5 Live and BBC Bitesize, we followed four students from Newcastle - Param, McKenzie, Jasmine and Javaris - as they tried out roles for the first time as part of their work experience placements.

articles.title: Paris estende toque de recolher após protestos violentos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo francês prepara operação de segurança de grande escala para manifestações convocadas para sábado, após dias de confrontos e saques; Paris, Lyon e Marselha adotaram restrições noturnas.
articles.summary: Paris, Lyon e Marselha adotaram restrições noturnas após episódios de violência na França. Governo prepara grande operação de segurança para protestos no sábado.
articles.body:
As autoridades francesas decretaram, nesta terça-feira (20), pelo segundo dia consecutivo, um toque de recolher das 23h00 às 6h00 na Place da República e na região comercial de Les Halles. As áreas foram os epicentros dos protestos ocorridos no último fim de semana .

O primeiro-ministro da França , Sébastien Lecornu, afirmou que o governo prepara uma operação de segurança de grande escala para novos protestos previstos para sábado (24).

A Polícia de Paris também proibiu qualquer concentração não autorizada a partir das 20h desta terça e até a madrugada da próxima quarta-feira (21) em áreas estratégicas, como a Champs-Élysées, estações ferroviárias e as sedes da Presidência francesa e do Parlamento.

A polícia de Paris informou que o toque de recolher ajudou a restabelecer a ordem durante a noite. A medida continuará em vigor pelo tempo que for necessário.

As restrições não abrangem outras áreas atingidas pelos confrontos no sábado, como a avenida Champs-Élysées, os arredores da estação ferroviária Saint-Lazare e trechos da Rue de Turbigo, no centro da capital. Nessas regiões, manifestantes montaram barricadas e atearam fogo.

Em Lyon, uma das maiores cidades francesas, as autoridades renovaram o toque de recolher no centro, das 21h às 6h. Segundo o governo local, não houve incidentes durante a noite.

Manifestante joga objeto contra policiais na França — Foto: Stephanie Lecocq/Reuters

Marselha, segunda maior cidade do país, determinou um toque de recolher para menores de idade desacompanhados, com início na noite desta terça.

Sindicatos estudantis e grupos ligados ao movimento dos coletes amarelos, que protagonizou protestos contra os preços dos combustíveis em 2018 e 2019, convocaram uma nova jornada de manifestações para sábado.

O ministro do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, informou nesta terça-feira a parlamentares que soldados da operação Sentinelle, criada para combater o terrorismo e reforçar a segurança após os ataques do grupo Estado Islâmico em 2015, passarão a proteger locais considerados sensíveis.

A medida busca liberar policiais e integrantes da gendarmaria, força de segurança com atribuições policiais e militares, para atuar no controle das manifestações.

"O efetivo mobilizado no próximo sábado será enorme", afirmou Lecornu à Assembleia Nacional, a Câmara baixa do Parlamento francês. O primeiro-ministro não informou quantos agentes serão mobilizados.

articles.title: Profissões em alta na Baixada Santista 2027: salários de R$ 83 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento da Robert Half revela os cargos mais disputados, os setores mais aquecidos, tendência de remuneração. Região da Baixada Santista se destaca pela atividade portuária e comércio internacional.
articles.summary: Profissões em alta na Baixada Santista em 2027 incluem cargos em tecnologia e logística com remunerações de até R$ 83,8 mil, segundo estudo da Robert Half.
articles.body:
Vagas de emprego — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/ Agência Brasil

Um levantamento feito pela consultoria Robert Half aponta que as áreas de Compras , Planejamento , Materiais , Comercial e Tecnologia devem liderar as contratações na Baixada Santista em 2027.

O levantamento mostra ainda quais cargos estarão em alta e uma previsão dos salários das vagas, com remunerações de até R$ 83,8 mil. O levantamento considera o cenário do litoral sul de São Paulo. Veja detalhes abaixo:

Ainda segundo a pesquisa, os setores de Infraestrutura, Logística, Ativos portuários e comércio internacional, Agronegócio e Tecnologia serão os segmentos mais aquecidos no estado no próximo ano.

Profissionais mais requisitados na Baixada Santista em 2027

Desenvolvedor/Engenheiro(a) de software relacionado à área de IA

De acordo com a pesquisa, o município de Santos (SP) atrai investimentos estrangeiros nos setores portuário, de comércio internacional, agronegócio e logística, impulsionados também por operações de fusões e aquisições (M&A)

“A agenda de M&A reforça esse movimento, enquanto Santos começa a desenvolver um ecossistema de tecnologia e IA, ainda menor que outros polos nacionais", comentou Leonardo Berto, gerente da operação da Robert Half na Baixada Santista.

Salários mais altos da Baixada Santista em 2027

Entre as carreiras com os maiores salários previstos para 2027 na Baixada Santista, destacam-se os cargos executivos de vendas e marketing e do mercado financeiro. Veja o top 10 dos cargos mais bem pagos em 2027:

Gerente Geral (G) - Vendas e Marketing: até R$ 83,8 mil

Chief Data Officer (CDO) - Mercado Financeiro: até R$ 80 mil

Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Mercado Financeiro: até R$ 78,5 mil

Diretor Financeiro (CFO) (G) - Finanças e Contabilidade: até R$ 78,4 mil

Chief Operating Officer (COO) - Mercado Financeiro: até 77,7 mil

Diretor Executivo/Chief Risk Officer (CRO) - Mercado Financeiro: até R$ 75,5 mil

Chief Data Officer (CDO) - Seguros: até R$ 72 mil

Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Seguros: até R$ 70 mil

Diretor Executivo de Relacionamento - Mercado Financeiro: até R$ 65,950 mil

Diretor Geral - Mercado Financeiro: até R$ 62,5 mil

Os salários apresentados representam remunerações iniciais praticadas no mercado e não incluem bônus, participação nos lucros ou outros benefícios.

A Robert Half divide as faixas salariais em três percentis, que variam conforme a experiência, a qualificação e a demanda de mercado para cada profissional.

25º percentil: profissional novo na função, com pouca ou nenhuma experiência, que precisa de mais instruções ou supervisão para realizar as tarefas diárias.

50º percentil: profissional com experiência para desempenhar as principais responsabilidades de forma consistente, sem supervisão direta, e familiarizado com os processos e assuntos relacionados ao cargo.

75º percentil: profissional cujo valor para a organização vai além da execução das tarefas habituais, com qualificações diferenciadas, especializações ou certificações e preparo para avançar na carreira.

As letras “P”, “M” ou “G” (pequeno, médio ou grande), que acompanham alguns cargos, representam o faturamento das empresas. Uma empresa grande é aquela com faturamento acima de R$ 500 milhões.

articles.title: Bugatti restaura único Veyron 'espelhado' | G1
articles.standfirst: Raro Grand Sport Vitesse tem carroceria de alumínio, interior de couro vermelho e passou por um processo de recuperação. Bugatti tem 1.200 cv e pode passar dos 400 km/h.
articles.summary: Raro Grand Sport Vitesse tem carroceria de alumínio, interior de couro vermelho e passou por um processo de recuperação. Bugatti tem 1.200 cv e pode passar dos 400 km/h
articles.body:
Bugatti restaurou o Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse com carroceria de alumínio polido. — Foto: Divulgação / Bugatti

A Bugatti restaurou um Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse com carroceria de alumínio polido , que já foi visto em Mônaco com o piloto de Fórmula 1 Fernando Alonso ao volante . O carro foi vendido recentemente pela empresa alemã Mechatronik, a mesma que vendeu o Pagani Zonda Roadster Diamante Verde a Alonso. (Veja mais detalhes a seguir)

O exemplar, identificado pelo número de chassi 8.100, voltou à sede da Bugatti, em Molsheim, na França, para passar por um processo de certificação, recuperação e reconfiguração. O objetivo era resgatar as características originais do projeto e preservar a história do modelo .

O trabalho foi feito pelo programa La Maison Pur Sang , criado pela fabricante para pesquisar o histórico dos carros, certificar sua autenticidade e realizar restaurações. Os valores do carro e da restauração não foram divulgados.

A iniciativa também auxilia colecionadores a encontrar modelos para suas coleções e permite que os veículos sejam recuperados de acordo com suas especificações originais ou modificados conforme a vontade dos proprietários.

No caso do Veyron de chassi 8.100, uma das etapas centrais foi retirar personalizações acrescentadas posteriormente . A intenção era recuperar a proposta original do carro, mantendo suas características históricas.

A montadora não detalhou quais peças foram substituídas ou reparadas durante o serviço. O trabalho divulgado, porém, incluiu a certificação do exemplar e a recuperação cuidadosa de sua configuração.

Fernando Alonso flagrado em Mônaco dirigindo o raro Bugatti Grand Sport Vitesse com carroceria de alumínio polido. — Foto: Reprodução / Redes sociais

O acabamento externo é o principal diferencial do Veyron. Em vez de esconder o metal sob uma pintura convencional, a carroceria utiliza alumínio polido exposto , que reflete a luz e cria o efeito espelhado nas superfícies do carro.

A solução exigiu um trabalho cuidadoso desde a fabricação. Blocos de alumínio que pesavam até 20 toneladas foram levados para Molsheim para viabilizar o projeto.

Antes de chegar à oficina, o desenho passou por estudos de proporções, superfícies e iluminação . Depois de definido o visual, o trabalho foi realizado no ateliê da Bugatti, onde profissionais especializados deram forma ao projeto.

A fabricante também documentou as etapas de criação, formando um registro do desenvolvimento de um dos projetos mais singulares da época do Veyron.

Por dentro, o carro combina couro vermelho Carmine Red , fibra de carbono aparente, alumínio polido e detalhes feitos à mão . O interior vermelho cria um contraste com a carroceria metálica.

Bugatti restaurou o Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse com carroceria de alumínio polido.

O Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse também se destaca pelo conjunto mecânico. O modelo usa um motor W16 de 8.0 litros , com quatro turbos, capaz de entregar 1.200 cv de potência e 153 kgfm de torque .

Mais de uma década depois de sua criação, o Veyron está na Riviera Francesa, região que inclui Mônaco.

A Bugatti descreve o exemplar como um dos mais raros Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse já produzidos.

Segundo Luigi Galli, especialista em patrimônio histórico e certificação da montadora, o programa busca acompanhar os colecionadores desde a pesquisa sobre a história de um veículo até a preservação de sua autenticidade para o futuro.

Pagani Zonda Roadster Diamante Verde do piloto de F1 Fernando Alonso. — Foto: Divulgação / Mechatronik

Outro carro raro ligado a Fernando Alonso é o Pagani Zonda Roadster Diamante Verde , um exemplar único que o piloto comprou também por meio da empresa alemã Mechatronik. Fabricado em 2017, o superesportivo tem motor V12 de 760 cavalos, carroceria com fibra de carbono aparente e pintura especial.

O nome Diamante Verde faz referência à combinação exclusiva de cores e acabamentos do carro. A configuração foi criada na própria fábrica da Pagani, seguindo as especificações da linha 760.

Não se trata de uma conversão feita posteriormente por uma empresa especializada, mas de uma unidade produzida originalmente com essas características.

O exemplar é um dos mais exclusivos da família Zonda e tinha apenas 800 quilômetros rodados quando foi entregue a Alonso.

Desde que saiu da fábrica, segundo a Mechatronik, teve somente um proprietário anterior, de acordo com o histórico.

Uma das principais diferenças do Diamante Verde está no conjunto externo. A carroceria combina fibra de carbono aparente com uma pintura especial , aplicada por um processo que não foi utilizado da mesma maneira em nenhum outro Pagani.

O capô dianteiro também chama a atenção. A peça foi originalmente desenvolvida para o Zonda 760LM, enquanto os para-lamas dianteiros são mais largos que os de outras configurações do superesportivo.

A construção utiliza um chassi que combina carbono e titânio , material que faz parte da estrutura do carro. O acabamento interno segue uma proposta mais discreta, com Alcantara preta.

Por ser um roadster, o modelo permite dirigir sem teto . Nessa configuração, os ocupantes ficam mais próximos do som produzido pelo motor e pela admissão de ar, que alimenta o V12 por meio de dutos conectados a uma entrada no estilo da configuração Cinque .

Pagani Zonda Roadster Diamante Verde do piloto de F1 Fernando Alonso.

O Pagani Zonda Roadster Diamante Verde é equipado com um motor Mercedes-AMG V12 de 7.3 litros. O conjunto entrega 760 cv de potência .

O sistema de escapamento também tem componentes específicos. Os coletores, com formato trabalhado e revestimento cerâmico, direcionam os gases para quatro silenciadores azulados de liga de inconel.

Na traseira, as quatro saídas ficam agrupadas dentro de um elemento circular, característica visual dos modelos da Pagani.

Pagani Zonda Roadster Diamante Verde de Fernando Alonso com capacete do piloto e cadeirinha personalizada. — Foto: Divulgação / Mechatronik

articles.title: Feriado em Petrolina: Dia do Servidor é transferido para 30 de outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Órgãos municipais, escolas e creches funcionarão normalmente na quarta-feira (28) e ficarão fechados na sexta-feira (30); serviços essenciais serão mantidos.
articles.summary: O feriado em Petrolina do Dia do Servidor foi transferido para 30 de outubro, alterando o funcionamento de escolas e órgãos municipais nesta semana.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Petrolina — Foto: Deivid Menezes

A Prefeitura de Petrolina , no Sertão de Pernambuco, transferiu o feriado do Dia do Servidor Público, celebrado em 28 de outubro, para o dia 30 deste mês. A mudança foi estabelecida por meio de decreto e tem como objetivo adequar o calendário de funcionamento da administração municipal.

Com a alteração, os órgãos públicos municipais, as escolas e as creches funcionarão normalmente na quarta-feira (28). Já na sexta-feira (30), não haverá expediente nesses locais.

Os serviços considerados essenciais à população serão mantidos durante o feriado. Entre eles estão o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), o Centro de Parto Normal (CPN) e os serviços de segurança, trânsito e limpeza pública.

A população também poderá acessar os serviços municipais pela plataforma Petro Online, disponível no site oficial da Prefeitura de Petrolina.

articles.title: Reform leader accuses MSP of 'squatting' in seat after resignation
articles.summary: Malcolm Offord says he is 'disappointed' at Amanda Bland's decision to leave the party and sit as an independent.
articles.body:
The leader of Reform UK in Scotland has accused an MSP of "squatting" in a Holyrood seat won by the party.

Malcolm Offord said Amanda Bland did not have a "personal mandate" to stay in the Scottish Parliament after she resigned from Reform to sit as an independent.

Bland, who was elected as a list MSP for Central Scotland and Lothians West in May's, denied claims she had stood down after being called to a meeting about high turnover among her office staff.

Offord said he was "disappointed" by her decision but Reform "wanted people who could work as a team".

Bland's departure relegates the party to third-largest in the Holyrood chamber, behind the SNP and Labour.

Offord told BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast he had not spoken to Bland since she announced her departure from the party.

Reform MSP quits party to sit as independent

Conservative MSP Graham Simpson defects to Reform

Reform MSP Graham Simpson did not resign when he defected from the Scottish Conservatives in August 2025.

Offord said that situation was different as Simpson only had eight months of his term left before May's election, while Bland is just a few months into her five-year tenure.

"Amanda's got her own reasons and, clearly, I'm disappointed. But she feels she can make more impact standing as an independent," he said.

"She is now proposing to squat in a list place won by Reform for four-and-a-half years."

He added: "It just looks to the voting public like there is a distinction between a constituency, where I would say you have won a personal mandate. If you are a list MSP, you are there just on the vote for the party."

A Reform source told BBC Scotland Bland's departure came amid claims she was "difficult to work with".

She had allegedly been called to a meeting last week to discuss high staff turnover within her parliamentary office, but Bland denied her resignation came as a consequence of that.

In a statement, Bland said her "principles and priorities remain unchanged" and that she believed she could best pursue her goals of "holding the Scottish government to account" as an independent MSP.

Under Holyrood's rules, any list MSP who resigns their seat is replaced by their party's next candidate at the last election.

As Bland is remaining as the Scottish Parliament's sole independent, Reform now have 16 MSPs, one behind Labour's 17.

That means they will not receive joint billing as the main opposition during first minister's questions.

Offord described Reform's slip into third place as "irritating" but said it would not "derail" their objectives.

He said: "We want people who are talented and bright and Amanda is talented and bright, but we also want people who are prepared to work as a team.

"One of the great things we're doing at Reform is building a team."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage was asked about Bland's departure following an event in Plymouth.

He said he "did not know the reasons" behind her decision, but that "parties losing people was always regrettable".

Asked if Bland should stand down as an MSP, he said: "I don't know the circumstances yet, but probably, yes."

Offord said some in his party had been "surprised" by what he called the "poisonous atmosphere" at the Scottish Parliament.

Prior to their election, only former Conservative MSP Simpson had previous Holyrood experience.

Offord claimed other parties were "resentful" of Reform's presence in the chamber.

The party attracted widespread condemnation for tabling a debate about banning face-coverings, including burkas , from public places.

"We've been taken by surprise frankly, in Holyrood, by the amount of vitriol," he told the programme.

"It's a pretty poisonous atmosphere, quite a difficult atmosphere to be in. The other parties are very resentful of Reform being there.

"For the Reform folk coming in, some of them have been taken by surprise by the amount of unpleasantness around and some of have found it more difficult than others."

articles.title: Toledo’s 1897 railroad swing bridge was bought for $1 in 2004; a new $65 million overhaul will replace nine fixed spans and reinforce the movable section to carry heavier 286,000-pound railcars
articles.summary: An ageing railroad swing bridge over Ohio’s Maumee River is set for a $65 million overhaul that could expand freight capacity through Toledo, nearly 130
articles.body: An ageing railroad swing bridge over Ohio’s Maumee River is set for a $65 million overhaul that could expand freight capacity through Toledo, nearly 130 years after the structure was built. The Toledo Swing Bridge, historically known as the Toledo Belt Bridge, was acquired by Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway from Norfolk Southern for just $1 in 2004. According to the US Department of Transportation, the bridge has been awarded approximately $43.55 million in federal funding for modernisation, with the project intended to enable it to accommodate railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds. The remaining project costs will be covered by the railway and state support, with construction expected to begin in 2029.A century-old bridge with a strategic roleBuilt in 1897, the Toledo Swing Bridge crosses the Maumee River near the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority’s Ironville Dock. Its location makes it an important link between railway operations and the region’s industrial and port facilities. The bridge is owned by Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway, a regional freight operator that uses the structure to transport commodities including lumber, steel, scrap metal, petroleum products and industrial sand. According to The Blade, the railway currently runs approximately six trains a week across the bridge, carrying around 8,000 freight carloads annually.Despite its continued use, the bridge’s existing structural capacity restricts the types of railcars that can cross it. This creates a bottleneck for freight movements, limiting the railway’s ability to accommodate certain modern railcars and potential additional shipments. The planned rehabilitation is intended to address these limitations while preserving the bridge’s role in Toledo’s transport network.Why the bridge was sold for $1The bridge’s unusual ownership history dates back to the restructuring of American rail operations following the breakup of Conrail. Norfolk Southern acquired much of Conrail’s railway network in the Toledo area in 1999, including the bridge. However, Wheeling & Lake Erie had already been using the structure as its main route for certain connections. Norfolk Southern eventually proposed transferring ownership to Wheeling, which had become the bridge’s only regular user.A September 2004 report republished by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen said Norfolk Southern proposed selling the century-old structure for $1. The nominal price reflected the circumstances of the transfer, rather than the bridge’s importance as transport infrastructure. The Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority supported the transaction because it wanted the bridge to remain operational. Abandonment could have threatened its future and created complications for navigation on the river. Wheeling’s acquisition ensured that the structure remained available for freight operations. More than two decades later, the proposed overhaul represents a major investment in its long-term use.What the $65 million overhaul will changeThe rehabilitation will focus on the bridge’s fixed spans and its movable section, which swings to allow vessels to pass along the Maumee River. According to The Blade, the project will replace nine fixed spans and reinforce the movable section. The railway plans to strengthen the swing span and replace deteriorated steel components so that the bridge can support railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds, equivalent to 143 US short tons.The federal government’s project summary also includes the replacement of the bridge’s timber fender systems. The Ohio Rail Development Commission’s May 2026 project documents describe the replacement of ageing truss and timber spans, including a new span and an abutment outside the waterway, as well as strengthening the movable swing span. The project is expected to begin in 2029 and finish in 2030, subject to environmental approvals, final engineering and design.The project is estimated to cost approximately $65 million. Federal funding of approximately $43.55 million will cover about two-thirds of the total, while an Ohio Rail Development Commission grant of $1.5 million will contribute towards the cost. Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway will fund the remaining costs, estimated at approximately $20 million.How the upgrade could increase freight movementThe principal benefit of the project will be the bridge’s ability to accommodate heavier railcars, including configurations that are currently restricted. This could give Wheeling & Lake Erie greater flexibility in serving industrial customers and moving freight through Toledo. The railway has indicated that additional cargo opportunities could become viable once the bridge’s limitations are addressed. However, the project does not guarantee a specific increase in freight traffic, and future volumes will depend on demand and the railway’s commercial decisions.The investment is also part of a wider federal effort to improve rail infrastructure. On October 19, 2026, the US Department of Transportation announced more than $2.3 billion in funding for 105 rail projects across 45 states and the District of Columbia through its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements programme.For Toledo, the bridge project combines the preservation of historic infrastructure with a practical freight upgrade. A structure acquired for $1 in 2004 is now set to receive tens of millions of dollars in improvements, potentially strengthening the city’s connections between railways, industrial facilities and river transport.You use AI every day. articles.title: UK to deploy Typhoon jets to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Ministry of Defence says warplanes will operate in ‘defensive role’ and not be used to attack Yemeni group.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom has said it will deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi Arabia from attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

In a statement on Tuesday, the British Ministry of Defence said the Typhoon warplanes would operate in a “defensive role” and not carry out attacks against the Iranian-backed armed group.

“The UK will fly defensive counter air missions to support the protection of Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure against aerial attack, using RAF Typhoon fighter jets,” it added.

The support includes an extension of air-to-air refuelling support for Saudi air operations, the ministry added.

The announcement comes amid heavy fighting between the Houthis – also known as Ansar Allah, Arabic for Supporters of God – and Yemen’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.

In recent weeks, the Houthis have carried out missile and drone strikes against the kingdom, including oil facilities and Riyadh’s main airport, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the Yemeni government has launched air attacks on Houthi positions.

“The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region,” UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said.

“That’s why today I have approved further UK military support. RAF Typhoons will fly defensive air missions to help protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles. This builds on the UK equipment and personnel we already have in the country to defend against Houthi air attacks,” he added.

Reporting from London, Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec said the UK government’s decision was partly driven by growing concerns over rising energy prices.

“What’s happening in the Gulf has a direct impact on people’s homes,” she said, adding that the move “shows increasing engagement by the UK” in the region.

The UK announcement came a day after Egypt’s parliament delayed for a second day a vote on President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia, if the kingdom asked for its support.

State media said the new session would be held on October 26.

articles.title: Kim Jong Un: Why do rumours about his death keep coming back?
articles.summary: North Korean state media has published photos of the dictator with his daughter after the unsubstantiated rumour spread.
articles.body:
Kim Jong Un has appeared in North Korean state media looking remarkably healthy for a man rumoured to have died from a brain haemorrhage.

Photographs published by state newspaper Rodong Sinmun show the 42-year-old dictator touring what the paper said was a clothing and footwear exhibition with his daughter.

The images emerged hours after a Chinese dissident who lives in the US claimed, without evidence, that Kim had been taken to a hospital in Beijing in a coma and had died.

For those who watch North Korea closely, this kind of rumour has become almost routine.

In one of the world's most secretive states, facts are often difficult to verify, creating fertile ground for speculation.

This latest claim originated with Wanjun Xie, who identifies himself as chairman of the Chinese Democratic Party, a group banned by Chinese authorities. He has previously circulated unverified claims, including speculation about the death of Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Xie alleged that Kim suffered a severe brain haemorrhage and was transferred to Beijing because North Korea lacked the medical facilities to treat him.

He claimed Kim later died and that his body had been secretly returned to North Korea, with the regime concealing his death.

Yet the photographs tell a different story.

Kim is seen examining displays, accompanied by Kim Ju Ae and his usual entourage of officials.

While there is no way to know exactly when the images were taken, there are other reasons to doubt the claim.

There would probably be signs beyond North Korea's borders if there were a sudden collapse in Kim's health.

China could tighten security along its frontier to prepare for potential instability or refugee flows. Activity around North Korean diplomatic missions might also increase. Defectors in South Korea often receive information through informal networks along the Chinese border. None of this has happened.

South Korean intelligence officials, meanwhile, told Yonhap they had heard nothing to support the reports.

The rumour also echoes previous false alarms.

In 2020, a high-profile North Korean defector claimed he was "99% certain" Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Not long afterwards, Kim appeared in public and the claim unravelled.

So why do these rumours keep resurfacing? The first reason is succession.

North Korea has been ruled by the Kim family for three generations, but what happens after Kim Jong Un remains less certain than it was for his predecessors.

Kim Il Sung spent decades preparing his son, Kim Jong Il, for power. By the time Kim Il Sung died in 1994, the succession plan was firmly established. Kim Jong Il's transition was relatively smooth.

Kim Jong Un's rise was faster and more precarious. After Kim Jong Il suffered a stroke in 2008, his youngest son was rapidly promoted through the ranks. By the time his father died in 2011, he had been publicly identified as the future leader.

Even so, Kim Jong Un spent years consolidating power, purging rivals and eliminating perceived threats.

Today, South Korea's intelligence agency believes he may be preparing his daughter as a successor. She has increasingly appeared at high-profile events and military displays.

But she is thought to be only 13 years old. North Korea has never been led by a woman, and she has not been formally designated as heir. Her youth would also leave her vulnerable in any power struggle.

All of this uncertainty helps explain why rumours about Kim's health attract so much attention.

The second reason is that the rumours are not entirely implausible.

Kim is overweight and a heavy smoker. South Korea's National Intelligence Service has repeatedly warned that his lifestyle puts him at higher risk of cardiovascular disease. Heart problems and strokes also run in the Kim family.

If anything were to happen to Kim, the stakes are high for neighbouring countries and the wider international community. Any sudden leadership crisis raises difficult questions about control of North Korea's nuclear weapons and the prospect of political instability.

Would a power struggle tempt hardliners to act aggressively? Could unrest trigger a refugee crisis along the Chinese border? These are questions that concern not only Beijing and Seoul but also Washington, which maintains around 28,000 troops in South Korea.

Intelligence agencies watch Kim Jong Un closely so they are prepared for any news.

Because North Korea remains an information black hole, it is also an easy target for false reports. Only a tiny circle has regular access to its leader. Even intelligence agencies struggle to obtain reliable information, and much of what emerges is heavily caveated as unverified or highly likely rather than confirmed fact.

The regime itself is also suspected of deliberately encouraging confusion, leaking misleading information to obscure what is really happening inside the country.

So it is hard to believe that Wanjun Xie had somehow stumbled across such significant news, when it had eluded those whose job it is to stay across it.

He may simply have been seeking attention. Or he may have wanted to embarrass Beijing by highlighting its ties to Pyongyang, although those are well-established for the world to see.

Whatever his motive, Xie is far from the first person to exploit the uncertainty surrounding North Korea's leadership.

articles.title: Russia urges early resumption of nuclear stability talks with US in possible Putin-Trump-Xi summit
articles.summary: Moscow on Tuesday called for an urgent restart of dialogue with Washington on strategic nuclear stability, with Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warning
articles.body: Moscow on Tuesday called for an urgent restart of dialogue with Washington on strategic nuclear stability, with Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warning that the world is, for the first time in history, without a legal framework to govern the area.Peskov was responding to a query on a possible three-way meeting in China next month between Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. He said the complexity of the issues meant negotiations should begin at the earliest, as any such talks were bound to be prolonged.The Kremlin had earlier indicated that the three leaders could meet on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen next month. The disclosure followed a Wall Street Journal report claiming Putin was seeking the trilateral format to push a peace settlement favourable to Moscow.Trump open to meetingTrump signalled on Monday that he was prepared to travel to China for a meeting with Putin and Xi, adding that the agenda would centre on denuclearization, though the Ukraine war could also come up.Asked by reporters whether he would take part in a meeting with the two leaders to discuss Ukraine, Trump said: “I would do it, not so much for Ukraine, because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven’t been doing much.”“We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation,” he added, AFP reported.Beijing, meanwhile, did not confirm the plan. Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she had no information about any such meeting, AFP reported.Ukraine, however, has voiced strong reservations, arguing that a meeting held without its participation would work against efforts to end the war. Foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said on Monday that such a gathering would only embolden Putin to keep up the conflict.“A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Ukraine, the US, and Russia could help end the war sooner. A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, China, and the US would do only the opposite: encourage Putin to continue this war,” he said in a post on X.The Kremlin, for its part, acknowledged that a final peace agreement could not be reached without Ukraine’s involvement. Asked whether Putin believed a deal was possible without Kyiv at the table, Peskov said it was obvious that Ukraine would have to be part of any final settlement.“Of course, a final settlement is impossible without the participation of someone in Kyiv who is prepared to take responsibility,” he said, as cited by Reuters.You use AI every day. articles.title: Paddy Power cuts 1,400 jobs and blames betting tax rises
articles.summary: The government increased taxes on online casino and sports betting in last year's Budget.
articles.body:
Paddy Power-owner Flutter has announced plans to cut up to 1,400 jobs as its boss claimed the company "cannot fully absorb" tax rises imposed on the gambling industry.

Staff based in Leeds and Dublin, as well as workers for its UK and Ireland business at Flutter's Portugal and Romania sites, will be most affected, but what roles are at risk has not been disclosed.

The government announced taxes rises on online casino and sports betting, with an exemption for horse racing, in the Budget last year.

Flutter boss Kevin Harrington said the tax hikes had "fundamentally changed" the economic model of the UK betting and gaming industry, arguing it had helped "fuel the unlicensed, unregulated market".

"We continue to expect these tax increases to have a very significant impact on the overall market," Flutter Entertainment said on Tuesday.

Flutter, which also owns Sky Bet and Betfair, employs 28,500 people across the world, including 9,000 in the UK and Ireland.

As well as its Leeds and Dublin offices, the BBC understands the cuts could also affect staff based in London and Sunderland, as well as Malta and Gibraltar.

Harrington, who is chief executive of the betting giant's UK and Ireland business, said: "As we warned a year ago, we cannot fully absorb a rise of this magnitude without reducing our fixed cost base and therefore must restructure our business so that we can best position ourselves for the future."

A government spokesperson said the job cuts were a "commercial decision for Flutter, not the UK government".

"However, we understand this will be a difficult time for the workers," they added.

Flutter delisted from the London Stock Exchange in August in a blow to the UK, with its shares now solely traded in New York.

In its most recent results, the company reported a $299m (£224m) pre-tax loss for the three months to June for its entire business worldwide, compared to a $205m profit in the same period last year. Sales rose 3% to $4.3bn.

However, revenues in the UK and Ireland rose by 4% over the period, due to strong growth in online gambling games.

Some online gambling tax rises announced in last year's Budget took effect in April. This included remote gaming duty, which is paid on online casino betting, rising from 21% to 40%.

General betting duty, paid on the profits made from various forms of sports betting, was kept at 15% in betting shops, but is set to rise from 15% to 25% online in April next year.

Betting firms had warned that cost increases would lead to job losses and betting shop closures, but MPs dismissed the warnings as "scaremongering".

During the summer, Ladbrokes owner Entain announced job cuts, with news agency Reuters reporting 500 roles were being removed.

Punters' winnings from gambling are not taxed in the UK, nor is VAT charged on bets.

Flutter said its restructuring plan would cost between $80m and $90m.

The company has claimed in previous financial results that the impact of UK tax rises would hit its underlying profit by $320m this year and $540m in 2027, before any savings or restructure to mitigate the impact.

articles.title: In 1867, San Francisco minted a $5 gold coin that passed down through a family; 159 years later, it was found inside a cigar box in a Texas closet and sold for $97,600 after experts identified its rarity
articles.summary: An 1867 $5 gold coin made in San Francisco and forgotten inside a cigar box in a Texas closet has sold at auction for $97,600 (£74,800).
articles.body: An 1867 $5 gold coin made in San Francisco and forgotten inside a cigar box in a Texas closet has sold at auction for $97,600 (£74,800). The sale price was more than four times the coin's previous record. The coin, officially known as an 1867-S Liberty Half Eagle, was found during an estate appraisal in Buda, Texas. Appraisers discovered a green milk crate hidden in a bedroom closet. Inside were two shoeboxes and an old cigar box containing the historic coin and other 19th-century currency. According to auction details published by Heritage Auctions in Dallas, Texas, experts from the Professional Coin Grading Service (PCGS) examined the rare gold coin and gave it a Mint State 63 (MS63) grade. This confirmed it as the finest-known surviving example of this coin. It ranked two full grade points above the next best example. The coin was sold at Heritage Auctions' GACC U.S. Coins Signature event on October 8 and 9, 2026. It broke the previous auction record of $22,800 for the 1867-S coin.Civil War origins and family inheritanceFamily heirs said the coins originally belonged to their great-grandfather, a Union soldier who served during the American Civil War before settling in Columbus, Ohio. The gold coin was passed down through several generations before the family moved it to Texas. It remained stored in the closet for decades. In 1867, the San Francisco Mint produced only 29,000 Liberty Half Eagles. Many entered everyday use across the western frontier during the late 19th century. As a result, very few coins survived in their original mint condition. Experts at Heritage Auctions estimate that fewer than 100 examples of the 1867-S $5 gold coin survive today in any condition. Only two confirmed examples are known to remain in uncirculated Mint State condition.Bidding competition and rarity recognitionThe discovery of the coins in Buda changed the known rankings for the condition of 19th-century American gold coins. Before the October auction, the highest recorded public sale price for an 1867-S Liberty Half Eagle was $22,800. Heritage Auctions set that record in 2021. The coin's MS63 grade from PCGS attracted strong competition from private collectors and institutional investors, pushing the final price to $97,600. Todd Imhof, executive vice president of Heritage Auctions, explained the importance of the Texas discovery to the wider coin-collecting market. “When the finest certified example of a coin with this much historical significance comes to auction, collectors take notice,” Imhof said in an official press statement released by Heritage Auctions. Imhof added that finding an uncirculated 19th-century gold coin from a regional mint hidden in a home closet is extremely rare for today's appraisers.Broad auction highlights and market impactThe 1867-S $5 gold coin was part of a major two-day auction that brought in $19.39 million (£14.8 million) from U.S. coins and currency. According to official sales reports released by Heritage Auctions, the top item was a 1792 Half Disme graded MS68 PCGS, which sold for a record $2.928 million (£2.24 million). Other notable gold coin sales alongside the Texas discovery included:A 1907 Saint-Gaudens High Relief Double Eagle, Flat Rim, graded MS66 PCGS, which sold for $97,600.An 1861-O Liberty Double Eagle, AU53 PCGS CAC, made in New Orleans at the start of the Civil War, which sold for $91,500.An 1851 Augustus Humbert Fifty Dollar Gold Piece, AU58 NGC, produced during the California Gold Rush, which sold for $76,250.After the auction, the newly documented 1867-S half eagle became part of a private coin collection. This ended its 159-year journey from the San Francisco Mint to a bedroom closet in Texas.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Shakahola forest deaths: Paul Mackenzie's son says siblings were starved weeks before Kenya trial
articles.summary: Dan Mackenzie initially defended his father but now says he felt he had to report his own grandmother.
articles.body:
The eldest son of Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie, convicted of murdering 191 people, says his younger siblings were still being forced to fast as recently as two weeks ago.

Dan Mackenzie, 27, said he reported the case to police, who rescued eight children, including his five younger siblings from their grandmother's house, and took them to a rescue centre.

"They were basically forcibly fasted because they were denying food to them for almost three days," he tells BBC's Newsday.

His father was found guilty on Monday of murdering 190 children and one adult who starved to death in Shakahola forest, near the Kenyan coast.

He had ordered members of his doomsday cult to starve themselves and their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

Twenty-eight other cult leaders were also convicted of murder.

Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders

Dan Mackenzie, who had initially defended his father, said at first he had struggled to understand the allegations against the cult leader, but came to realise the scale of the tragedy during the court proceedings.

"When I was 12, I was forced to fast for almost a week," he says. He also remembers church members beating him for hours to make him attend a service as a child.

Now, he says he felt he had to report family members who still believe in the teachings in order to free his siblings. "I had to report my grandmother."

The cult leader's doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil".

"I left school when I was seven," says Dan.

Now living in the coastal town of Malindi, Dan earns a living as a motorcycle taxi driver, supporting himself and his younger siblings.

He said some people in the town had been angry with him because of his father's crimes, but others "had accepted him because he had distanced himself from that life".

"I hope the verdict would bring some comfort to those who had lost friends and relatives," Dan tells BBC's Newsday.

On Monday, Stephen Mwiti, 48, who said he had lost all six of his children to the cult, welcomed the verdict.

"I'm a happy man, that all persons have been convicted," he told the BBC outside court.

His former wife was one of those convicted of murder alongside Mackenzie.

Delivering her eight-hour judgment in the port city of Mombasa, Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece".

One of his co-accused told the court that Mackenzie had said anyone who resisted fasting must be forced to go to heaven "through kicks and blows".

Burials in the forest where the cult was based were described as "weddings", with those who died celebrated as having "wedded with Jesus", the judge said.

Mackenzie and other cult leaders also face separate cases involving terrorism, radicalisation and denying children an education.

The murder verdict is the first ruling on the most serious charges against the pastor, who was arrested in 2023 after more than 400 bodies were discovered in shallow graves in Shakahola forest, near Kenya's coast.

He is due to be sentenced on 6 November.

articles.title: Moment giant fin whale caught feeding off Pembrokeshire coast
articles.summary: Videographer Rhys Morgan captured footage of the worlds second largest whale  lunge feeding on his drone.
articles.body:
This is the moment the planet's second largest living creature opens its giant jaws and swallows thousands of gallons of water during feeding.

The fin whale was filmed by videographer Rhys Morgan off the Pembrokeshire coast in Wales, and it shows the mammal's expandable pleats take in up to 18,000 gallons of water and krill.

Morgan said "it was complete luck" that he captured the whale feeding and swimming with dolphins on his drone while fishing with a friend.

Second only to the blue whale, the fin whale is one of the largest animals ever to have lived, reaching up to 24m in length and weighing up to 70 tonnes.

Despite its enormous size, the fast-swimming creature is elusive and spends much of its life in the open ocean and often surfacing only briefly before disappearing beneath the waves.

The mammal can be found all over the world's oceans but is most at home in cooler waters.

Morgan, from Houghton, Pembrokeshire, works at an oil refinery by day, and said he was "brought up on the water", but became interested in marine videography after using his friends drone to capture footage of sea creatures across the surface of the ocean.

"It's pretty incredible really," Morgan said.

"It makes you feel very small out there."

To avoid causing harm to the whales while recording out at sea, Morgan said: "We do what we can to keep our distance in the boat but unfortunately nature can have a mind of its own sometimes.

"There's been times when we've been anchored up fishing with nothing happening in the area and a whale has popped up next to us.

"The wildlife will approach you sometimes."

Dr Marianna Chimienti is a lecturer in marine top predator ecology at Bangor University and said Morgan experienced a "rare and fortunate encounter".

Chimienti, who specialises in animal behaviour added: "It is normal that the fin whale comes and feeds at the surface, as it is part of the species foraging strategy but being in the coastal water is quite spectacular.

Little is known about fin whale migration but their movements are believed to be quite different from other baleen whales such as blues and humpbacks.

Scientists have found that fin whales are more abundant in higher latitudes in warmer months of the year, and more numerous in lower latitudes during colder months, but this can vary.

Fin whales have a pretty simple diet which is usually made up of krill, small schooling fish and squid.

Due to the small size of its prey, fin whales have to eat a lot to survive and can spend several hours each day feeding, consuming up to 2,000 kilograms of food.

articles.title: Yemen: Maps show 10 years of changing control
articles.summary: A decade of war has shifted Yemen’s front lines, but the Houthis still hold Sanaa, and no side controls the country.
articles.body:
Looking at maps of who controls which areas of Yemen over the past 12 years of war reveals changing alliances and coalitions, all while the country faces poverty and malnutrition.

The Houthi armed group, also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), seized the capital, Sanaa, on September 21, 2014, after advancing south from their heartland of Saada in northern Yemen.

The Iran-allied group used antigovernment grievances to gain support after July 2014 fuel subsidy cuts triggered anger.

The Houthis mobilised protests demanding the reversal of the government’s decisions, and subsequently its resignation. They allied with forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh, which helped them capture military positions and state institutions.

Then-President Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi fled to Aden in February 2015. When forces aligned with the Houthis and Saleh advanced towards the southern port city, Hadi took refuge in the Saudi capital, Riyadh. In March 2015, Saudi Arabia launched a military intervention to restore his internationally recognised government.

Over the next decade, alliances broke and front lines shifted. In this visual explainer, AJLabs uses seven maps to track how Yemen has been fragmented, and how no side has been able to control the whole country.

By late 2016, two years after the Houthis seized Sanaa, Yemen was split into rival zones of control.

The Houthi-Saleh alliance controlled Sanaa and much of the northern and western heartlands, home to most of Yemen’s population.

Pro-government forces held territory across the south and the east, supported by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) also challenged government authority across parts of the south.

The antigovernment alliance in Yemen went through its most significant fracture after Saleh appeared close to switching sides in the conflict, leading to a short outbreak of fighting with the Houthis, who then killed Yemen’s former longtime president in Sanaa in December 2017.

This left the Houthis, a primarily Zaidi Shia group, in sole charge of much of northwestern Yemen, including Sanaa and the port city of Hodeidah.

Some pro-Saleh forces switched sides, and pro-government and anti-Houthi forces controlled territory across the south and the east while AQAP retained pockets of influence.

Nearly three years into its intervention and despite a heavy air campaign, the Saudi-led coalition had failed to restore the internationally recognised government of Hadi in Sanaa.

The Houthis continued to hold Sanaa and much of the northwestern highlands. Government-aligned forces held extensive territory across the south and the east while AQAP maintained pockets of influence.

The December 2018 Stockholm Agreement halted a pro-government offensive against Houthi-held Hodeidah, a major entry point for food, fuel and aid.

Neither side had been able to achieve a decisive victory. Divisions among the Houthis’ opponents further weakened efforts to establish government authority.

The UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council (STC), which seized Aden in 2019, held territory separately from government forces. Despite officially being part of the anti-Houthi, Saudi-led coalition, the STC fought the government several times.

Hadi was forced to transfer his powers to an eight-member Presidential Leadership Council (PLC), ending his presidency without reclaiming the capital.

Saudi-Houthi negotiations raised hopes of a settlement and led to a truce in April 2022, but Yemen remained divided as it had been for years.

While the Houthis retained their control over Yemen’s northwest, the STC continued to undermine Yemen’s internationally recognised government as it tried to increase its own power in the south in the hope that this would eventually lay the foundations for an independent state.

Government forces controlled broad areas of the east, which separatists also wanted to claim for any future state.

The Hadrami Elite Forces, a UAE-backed group, controlled coastal Hadramout. The National Resistance Forces (NRF), led by Saleh’s nephew Tareq Saleh and supported by the UAE, held part of the Red Sea coast.

By 2025, the Houthis had held Sanaa and most of Yemen’s northwest continuously for more than a decade.

Government-aligned forces operated across the south and the east.

Houthi attacks on shipping, which the group said were launched in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza, drew attacks from Israel, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Yemen’s coastline and the Bab al-Mandeb strait became central to a confrontation whose consequences reached far beyond the country.

Government forces regained Hadramout and al-Mahra from the STC, which had seized the governorates in December 2025.

Saudi air attacks and a government advance fractured the STC’s leadership. A delegation in Riyadh announced the STC’s dissolution, but coalition officials in Yemen rejected the announcement, and its leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi fled the country.

The map above shows contested authority across parts of southern Yemen and Socotra. Tareq Saleh’s forces remain separately marked along the western coast while the Houthis retained Sanaa and the northwest.

The PLC sought to unify anti-Houthi formations. Regaining territory strengthened its position, but establishing a single command remained unfinished.

In early September, Houthi forces attacked west of Taiz in an attempt to cut road access to the Red Sea coast.

Government forces initially claimed gains in Hais and western Taiz, but the port city of Mocha fell on September 10 as Tareq Saleh’s NRF withdrew and repositioned.

By September 11, government sources reported Houthi advances into Dhubab and Mayyun Island, completing their reported takeover of Yemen’s Red Sea coast.

By September 25, nearly 130,000 people, including 71,000 children, had been displaced in three weeks, according to UNICEF.

PLC Chairman Rashad al-Alimi called for a general mobilisation and offered amnesty to Houthi fighters who defected.

Government forces intensified their air and ground operations in Taiz towards the end of the month while Saudi Arabia sought support from Pakistan and Turkiye amid continuing Houthi attacks.

After announcing Operation Dawn of Yemen on October 4, the internationally recognised government launched a major offensive on October 5 with the stated aim of retaking areas that included Sanaa. The Southern Giants Brigades fought alongside government troops and former STC-affiliated units.

The same day, the government said its forces had recaptured positions around Dhubab and Bab al-Mandeb, but the full extent of their gains on the coast could not be confirmed. It also said it had seized mountain positions in Haifan, western Taiz and around al-Waziiya.

Fighting also spread to Marib, where government forces claimed heights around the Maas camp and positions north of Harib by October 13.

But while the government claimed these gains, it also lost territory in Taiz governorate, leading to a siege on the city of Taiz, one of the most important government-held areas of the country, with the major road linking it to the south controlled by the Houthis.

The escalation deepened Yemen’s humanitarian crisis, and by October 7, more than 200,000 people had been displaced, including more than 3,700 who fled by sea to Djibouti, according to the International Organization for Migration.

Government and Saudi-led coalition air attacks increased, including on Sanaa. The Houthis, meanwhile, attacked Saudi Arabia repeatedly with ballistic missiles, including an October 10 attack on Riyadh’s airport that killed 13 people.

articles.title: ‘Horizontal revolt’: Why Albania’s young protesters want PM Rama to go
articles.summary: From the ‘Flamingo Revolution’ to current protests, an inside look at a leaderless youth uprising challenging Edi Rama.
articles.body:
For several days, the streets of Tirana have witnessed a wave of antigovernment demonstrations, with demonstrators engaged in fierce clashes with security forces, while police have fired tear gas on thousands of young protesters to prevent them from scaling barricades.

Protests escalated last week after school and university students joined them, citing rising tuition fees and crumbling infrastructure.

What initially began as a targeted environmental protest in May has rapidly escalated into one of the most serious political challenges facing Prime Minister Edi Rama in his more than a decade in power.

Yet, as the unrest reaches a boiling point, a fundamental question remains: Who is behind this movement, and can it force systemic political change?

Contrary to claims by government officials that the unrest is being orchestrated by political opponents or external actors, analysts and journalists on the ground emphasise that the movement is largely decentralised and youth-driven.

Fatos Hakorja, editor-in-chief of TV Klan and Klan News, told Al Jazeera that the demonstrations have evolved organically into a broad coalition of high school students, university students, environmentalists, and aggrieved citizens.

“So far, what can be said with certainty is that the protests have been organised mainly by young people themselves,” Hakorja told Al Jazeera. “What began as the ‘Flamingo Revolution’ gradually developed into a broader student and youth protest… There is no clear evidence that a single consolidated structure stands behind the protests,” he said, referring to the May protest against a luxury resort that threatens the protected coastline.

Hakorja noted that coordination takes place dynamically across digital platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, and Snapchat, rather than through formal organisational hierarchies.

Albanian political analyst and publicist Ben Andoni echoed this view, describing the situation not merely as a standard protest, but as “a genuine, horizontal revolt”.

“The protest has turned into a rebellion for the past seven days. It was a protest before, but it has never taken on the character of a movement. If it were so, there would be a leadership group and some short-, medium-, and long-term goals,” Andoni told Al Jazeera.

“It is a horizontal movement, where people are mobilised by TikTok groups and social networks, but not by true cultural and political organisations. That is also a handicap or a source of pressure for Rama’s government, which seeks to negotiate, but finds no single counterpart standing in its way.”

The roots of the current unrest are multifaceted, blending localised grievances with deep-seated frustration over governance, economic stagnation, and corruption.

The initial spark – dubbed the “Flamingo Revolution” – was ignited by environmental opposition to controversial luxury development projects, notably in the protected area of Zvernec and the planned resort investment on Sazan Island by the firm of Jared Kushner, United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law.

The flamingo, native to these coastal lagoons, quickly became a symbol of resistance against the perceived commodification of public lands.

However, environmental concerns swiftly converged with student anger over high tuition fees, inadequate dormitory conditions, and low educational competitiveness. Beneath these immediate triggers lies a much deeper structural crisis.

“Problems of corruption, nepotism, and a lack of perspective are the main reasons that drove people to protest,” Andoni explained.

“The protest summarised the entire range of problems that Albania has, and brought them to the doorstep of a government that has crossed lines regarding corruption, inequality, and particularly a lack of empathy for the people.

“Among some protesters, especially on social media, there is also a narrative that Rama is placing the country’s interests at the service of private interests, his personal hold on power, or foreign interests, including Israeli interests. These claims have not been proven, but they seem to have increased the anger of some young people and part of the wider population,” Hakorja added.

Rama has strongly rejected the allegations, calling them conspiracy theories and dismissing them as manipulated disinformation spread through social media by “foreign hands”, aimed at destabilising the government and undermining the country’s public institutions.

A defining feature of the uprising is the protesters’ explicit rejection of the ruling Socialist Party (SP) and the traditional opposition, including the Democratic Party (PD) led by Sali Berisha.

While Prime Minister Rama has accused the opposition of taking over the movement, and opposition supporters have joined the crowds on the ground, experts stress that opposition leaders exercise no direct control over the demonstrators. In fact, several opposition MPs who attempted to address the crowds faced open hostility and rejection.

“A large number of these young people seem to feel unrepresented by the whole political class,” Hakorja told Al Jazeera.

“They see the political system as disconnected from their reality and as a system that protects the interests of a minority more than it addresses the problems of the majority of citizens.”

This widespread cynicism has resulted in an uncompromising stance. Demonstrators have demanded the immediate resignation of Prime Minister Rama and the formation of a technical government, refusing official offers of dialogue due to a total breakdown of trust in state institutions.

The deep cynicism towards Albania’s political class stems from a widespread feeling that leaders are entirely indifferent to citizens’ daily struggles. Young people face rampant corruption, high unemployment, and an economy that drives huge brain drain.

This disconnect is further spurred by years of government apathy towards crumbling public education, high tuition fees, and poor dormitory conditions.

Furthermore, controversial state-backed developments – such as the planned luxury resort by Kushner’s firm – serve as prime examples for citizens who believe the political establishment consistently trades national resources and public goods for private and foreign interests.

Heavy-handed security and growing fatigue

Faced with a leaderless movement that refuses to negotiate, the Albanian government has increasingly relied on security forces to maintain control.

Police have been accused of brutality as they have used tear gas, water cannons, and rubber bullets to quell the protesters. At least 167 people have been arrested, including minors.

In a move that highlights the administration’s reliance on law enforcement, Prime Minister Rama announced a 2,500-euro ($2,800) bonus for police officers on the front lines, alongside substantial salary increases set for 2027.

Hakorja pointed out that the government is treating the crisis predominantly as a matter of public order and security.

He also highlighted troubling incidents, such as the appearance of unidentified civilians armed with wooden sticks inside the Socialist Party headquarters. While these individuals remained inside to protect the building as protesters hurled stones and attacked the entrance, their presence – including individuals holding public positions – led to fears of informal, non-state security responses operating alongside or outside official police forces.

As both sides brace for further escalation, the immediate outlook remains uncertain. Without clear leadership to negotiate terms, or intervention from international partners such as the European Union and the US, the deadlock threatens to prolong political instability.

According to Andoni, the Rama administration has used force as its main instrument, as it has suffered a severe loss of moral authority and legitimacy.

“Demonstrators remain persistent and aggressive, while Rama plays the card of force through the police,” Andoni told Al Jazeera, adding that “fatigue” is impacting the young protesters.

“It seems that young people may execute a tactical withdrawal first by temporarily stepping back from the streets due to exhaustion, leaving the weight and burden of proof on Mr Rama” – placing the ultimate responsibility on the prime minister to prove that his government has the legitimacy, capability, and sincere intent to carry out deep reforms and resolve a crisis that police force has only further escalated.

Whether this youth-led rebellion marks the beginning of a new political era in Albania or subsides under policing and exhaustion, it has irrevocably exposed the deep rift between Albania’s youth and its governing political establishment.

articles.title: Offshore nor’easter creating high surf and coastal flooding along the East Coast
articles.summary: A strengthening nor’easter hundreds of miles off the Atlantic will still manage to bring several days of gusty onshore winds and coastal flooding, along with some rain that could clip Cape Cod.
articles.body: A strengthening nor’easter hundreds of miles off the Atlantic will still manage to bring several days of gusty onshore winds and coastal flooding, along with some rain that could clip Cape Cod. The storm is expected to stay far enough offshore that the heaviest rain will likely affect only the easternmost parts of the country. While the rain will stay mostly offshore, gusty winds and coastal flooding are still possible, especially across the Outer Banks. Flood advisories are in place from the Jersey Shore to the Outer Banks for 1-2 feet of inundation from onshore winds. The storm, still offshore, is intensifying. Coastline cities from New Jersey to Cape Hatteras can expect coastal flooding, beach erosion and gusty winds. Rain and coastal flooding are expected to impact Cape Cod and Nantucket in the coming days. By Thursday, rough surf and rip currents will hit those areas. The nor’easter could become a tropical storm but, if it does, it will only intensify as it continues east and away from the coast. It has a 40% chance of formation in two days, and 40% in seven days. If it develops, it will be named Josephine. Winds will have the biggest impact, with 44 mph winds forecast in Nantucket. Virginia Beach could see 32 mph winds, and Cape Hatteras is expected to have 39 mph winds. Meanwhile, a storm in the Pacific Ocean is expected to bring heavy rain, flooding and mountain snow. A flash flood risk is in place from Southern California to the Rockies. A flood threat is in place for California and parts of the Southwest through Thursday, specifically in Southern California from San Luis Obispo to Santa Barbara, and across the Four Corners states. articles.title: ‘Every day could cost lives’: UK government blocks Gaza families’ reunion
articles.summary: Britain’s reopened refugee resettlement scheme offers no escape for Palestinians in Gaza.
articles.body:
When his three-year-old son asks why they cannot be together, his Palestinian father tells him the border is closed.

“He asks me, why don’t you open it?” the father, who requested anonymity, told Al Jazeera. “He thinks I own an airplane. He is always asking me, can you come and take us?”

Separated by Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, they speak over WhatsApp whenever the internet connection allows. The father has been granted protection in Britain, while his wife and their two children, remain trapped in a tent in Gaza.

“When I can’t get in touch with my wife, I feel so stressed. I am so scared that something bad has happened to her or the children.”

Sometimes, he goes to the park to clear his head, and sees children playing with their parents.

“My heart hurts when I see that,” he said. “I am incredibly lonely. Without my family it is impossible to enjoy anything. I worry about them all the time.”

Lawyers and rights groups estimate there are between 250 and 300 people who are seeking through the courts to have their immediate family join them from Gaza but remain separated.

On September 30 , an Upper Tribunal ruled to reunite the families in the UK, but the Home Office is appealing the decision and is refusing to waive the requirement for the families to provide biometrics, despite there being no registration facility in Gaza.

This is prolonging their separation as Israel continues to bombard the enclave despite a so-called ceasefire agreement in October 2025.

A second family that spoke to Al Jazeera also requested anonymity.

Earlier this month, shrapnel from an Israeli bomb damaged their home. The mother told Al Jazeera they have since been displaced again.

“Where we are now, there is no safety. They bombed the area next to us last night,” she said.

“I sat in the corner and I brought all three children to my body. They were all screaming and crying and I kept telling them everything will be OK.”

Asked what she would like most in the world, her youngest daughter answers: “To go to my baba with my sisters and my mama.”

Decla Palmer, a solicitor at Greater Manchester Immigration Aid Unit who represents the families, told Al Jazeera: “To hold your children and keep them safe from harm is the most basic wish of any parent. What these families are going through is every parent’s worst nightmare”.

“The fathers, in the UK, are facing the prospect that they may never hold their children again.”

Both families applied before the government suspended new applications under the refugee family reunion route on September 4, 2025.

Their lawyers say the families meet the requirements, but what keeps them apart is a bureaucratic catch-22.

They cannot obtain visas without providing biometrics. But Gaza’s visa application centre, where families would register physical characteristics such as fingerprints, has been closed since October 2023, so they cannot leave Gaza.

More flexible biometric requirements are given for those who need to be medically evacuated from Gaza, while the government has helped scholarship students leave Gaza and complete biometric checks in Jordan.

But lawyers say the Home Office is refusing to provide the same guarantees for separated family members to make that journey, even though they would still have to undergo UK and Israeli security checks.

Palmer said: “The Home Office is actively keeping these families apart, leaving them stranded in Gaza in grave danger.”

“The judge made the right decision in our case, ruling that the Home Office should apply its unsafe journeys policy lawfully to allow the mothers and children we represent, who are eligible to come to the UK under the Immigration Rules, to leave Gaza and reunite in the UK,” Palmer added.

“Instead, the Home Office is doing everything possible to delay and to defend its unlawful decisions, taking a policy position that blocks people in Gaza who are eligible to come to the UK from being able to do so.”

No safe and legal route for families inside Gaza

Activists say a dedicated Gaza family scheme could overcome these barriers, pointing to earlier arrangements that allowed eligible Ukrainians to provide biometrics after arriving in Britain.

A petition calling for such a scheme attracted more than 100,000 signatures and was debated in parliament in May 2024. In its December 2023 response, the government said it had no plans for bespoke arrangements, directing people towards existing visa routes.

Lawyers are now calling on the government to remove the obstacles preventing eligible families from reuniting under the existing visa route.

Since Israel closed Gaza’s Rafah crossing with Egypt in May 2024, lawyers say that no family has been reunited through the visa route these families are required to use, despite the UK government adopting a stronger position on Israel under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

This month, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood announced the reopening of the UK Resettlement Scheme, with the Home Office expecting new referrals to include Palestinian refugees. The news was met with rapturous applause at the Labour Party conference and was initially praised by pro-Palestine groups.

But the umbrella alliance, Communities for Palestinians (CFP), said Mahmood’s speech and subsequent Home Office statements failed to mention a key detail: that the Palestinian programme covers only a small number of exceptionally vulnerable refugees already in Jordan or Lebanon, meaning it does not apply to mothers and children trapped in Gaza.

Lawyers say that the only remaining safe and legal routes to the UK are if a Palestinian is severely injured by Israel and can be medically evacuated, or if they qualify for a student scholarship.

“There is a real contradiction in what we are seeing,” Ghassan Ghaben, senior community advocacy officer at the British Palestinian Committee, told Al Jazeera. “The Home Secretary has recently announced the reopening of the UK Resettlement Scheme, and spoken about creating safe and legal routes for people fleeing persecution. Yet at the same time, the Home Office is continuing to fight against the reunification of Palestinian mothers and young children with their fathers who are already in the UK.”

He says that for these families, the consequences are measured in lives.

“The government needs to stop treating this as an ordinary administrative problem. These are families separated by genocide, and every additional day of delay could cost them their lives.”

At the time of publishing, the Home Office had not responded to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

articles.title: More than 250,000 displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated: UNHCR
articles.summary: UNICEF says escalating fighting in Taiz is threatening its water systems, serving an estimated three million people.
articles.body:
More than 250,000 people have been internally displaced in Yemen since the country’s war reignited in July, the United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) has said, as fighting between Houthi rebels and forces loyal to the internationally recognised government rages across several fronts.

The city of Taiz in southwestern Yemen is at the centre of the displacement crisis, accounting for 76 percent of departures and hosting 52 percent of those newly displaced, UNHCR said in a statement on Tuesday.

Lahij in southwestern Yemen hosts 23 percent of the newly displaced population, followed by Aden in the south with 13 percent, UNHCR said.

“Shelling intensified in Taiz, including in residential areas and around health facilities, while insecurity and restrictions along key routes continue to constrain humanitarian access and movement,” the agency said in a statement.

The Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, the interim capital of the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government.

“The most immediate needs that we’ve been able to identify are around shelter, food, and multi-purpose cash assistance,” UNHCR spokesperson Matthew Saltmarsh told a news conference in Geneva, Switzerland.

The agency said about 33,700 families still require shelter assistance amid severe underfunding of the humanitarian response to the war.

Separately, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said in a statement that escalating fighting and fuel shortages in Taiz are threatening its water systems that serve an estimated three million people, including at least 1.6 million children.

“Already one of Yemen’s most water-scarce areas, Taiz is now facing renewed pressure on its most essential services for thousands of displaced families,” said Akhil Iyer, UNICEF’s Yemen representative, at a press briefing in Geneva.

The warnings come as fighting intensifies between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The death toll from a Houthi ballistic missile strike on a military training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa governorate increased to at least 58, local authorities said.

The Yemeni government described the site as a security training centre away from the front lines, while Houthi forces said they targeted Saudi-backed forces. Hospitals faced blood shortages in Ataq as medical teams responded to casualties and families searched for missing relatives.

The attack was followed by retaliatory strikes by government forces near Taiz, raising further concerns over the worsening humanitarian crisis in Yemen.

Reporting from the capital, Sanaa, Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry said, “The Houthis are not backing down. Their military spokesman says they are continuing to conduct more missile attacks deep inside Saudi Arabia.”

“As cross-border attacks grow, Yemenis fear the war is coming closer to home, especially as both sides threaten to escalate their attacks, while Saudi Arabia steps up its air campaign,” Mawry added.

Meanwhile, Yemen’s Saudi-backed coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said on Tuesday that its forces have destroyed 127 Houthi weapons depots and missile launch platforms.

Separately, the United Kingdom said it would deploy Royal Air Force jets ⁠on defensive missions to help protect Saudi Arabia from increasing Houthi ⁠attacks.

The British Ministry of Defence said in a statement that the Typhoon warplanes would operate in a “defensive role” and not carry out attacks against the Houthis.

Tensions have soared in Yemen since July, when the Houthis announced a blockade of Saudi ports, and fighting escalated sharply last month when they seized strategic territory from forces loyal to the government along the Red Sea coast.

Government forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, responded to the losses with a counteroffensive and launched Operation Dawn of Yemen, which aims to recapture Houthi-held territory, including Sanaa, seized by the group in 2014.
