articles.title: Trump official claims record-breaking 300,000 visas were revoked
articles.summary: The revocations targeted US visa holders who had allegedly broken the law, a spokesperson said.
articles.body:
The Trump administration has said it has revoked more than 300,000 visas issued to foreign nationals, claiming it has done so at a faster pace than any previous administration.

A spokesman for the US Department of State said on social media on Tuesday that the revocations targeted foreign nationals in the United States on visas who had broken the law, committed fraud or posed threats to national security.

“We have zero tolerance for foreigners here on visas who break the law, commit fraud, or undermine our national security,” Tommy Pigott, State Department spokesman, said in a post on the social media platform X .

The administration would continue taking action to secure US borders and protect national security, he added.

Al Jazeera has reached out to the State Department for comment.

The number of visa revocations exceeded 175,000 in August.

In January, the department said it had revoked more than 100,000 visas, a record at the time.

The administration has also adopted a stricter policy on granting visas, with tightened social media vetting and expanded screening.

Rights advocates and human rights experts have condemned the Trump administration’s social media screening efforts, which they say threaten free speech and are akin to surveillance and the singling out of immigrants.

articles.title: CBS boss fuels left-wing uproar amid report she urged staff to probe alleged El-Sayed, Muslim Brotherhood ties
articles.summary: Bari Weiss reportedly pushed CBS News journalists to investigate Abdul El-Sayed's alleged Muslim Brotherhood ties, sparking backlash from far-left critics.
articles.body: CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss is taking heat from the left yet again, this time over a report urging her staff to probe Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's potential ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. Semafor reported Sunday that Weiss "personally advocated for CBS News journalists to pursue numerous story angles related to El-Sayed’s supposed sympathy towards the Muslim Brotherhood." The report cited two anonymous CBS News staffers who were aggrieved by Weiss' directive. Anonymous CBS News staffers complaining about their boss to liberal media outlets has become commonplace in the media industry. CONTROVERSY OVER ABDUL EL-SAYED'S FAMILY TIES TO MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD IGNORED, DOWNPLAYED BY LIBERAL MEDIA NewsBusters executive editor Tim Graham believes disgruntled CBS News employees constantly offering anonymous quotes to liberal publications in an effort to smear Weiss "helps reinforce" the longstanding bias toward the left. "She’s making them do difficult things," Graham told Fox News Digital. "Can we look into whether Abdul El-Sayed has ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, like his family says they do? How dare you," Graham quipped. "You’re not supposed to do stories that might make Democrats look bad." While Weiss’ defenders have suggested staffers are essentially irked that she asked them to do journalism, progressives lashed out against Weiss over the latest report. "A rightwing, pro-Israel, anti-Muslim troll who has zero qualifications to be running national TV network is in fact running a national TV network and trying to get it to behave like a rightwing, pro-Israel, anti-Muslim troll," far-left Zeteo founder and former MSNBC host Mehdi Hasan reacted on X. "No self-respecting journalist should work for Bari Weiss," The Nation correspondent Jeet Heer wrote. "Nobody should respect or trust ANYTHING coming out of @CBSNews at this point," far-left activist Shaun King exclaimed. Notably, CBS News largely refrained from covering the controversy that blew up last week when unearthed social media posts from his half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, claimed their family, including their mother, had ties to the controversial Islamist group after he flatly denied there was any connection to NBC's Kristen Welker. "Had an amazing talk with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood during the early 70s while she was in college #respect," Abdelhadi wrote in a 2012 X post, as first reported by the Washington Free Beacon. Their mother, Fatten Elkomy, had attended Egypt's Alexandria University, which, according to a report from the Brookings Institution, had strong Muslim Brotherhood activity back in the 1970s. In another 2012 post, Abdelhadi, a professor at the University of Chicago, wrote, "My family has long been MB, but I've always felt that it has navigated the political sphere poorly/destructively." In a third post from 2013, she wrote, "Praying for all my family that supports the #MB in #Egypt. Lie low, stay safe." ABDUL EL-SAYED GROWS AGITATED WITH REPORTER AFTER BEING PRESSED ON FAMILY'S ALLEGED MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES Graham feels that CBS News staffers who didn’t want to look into the El-Sayed story must find it "wildly offensive" to even consider a conservative point of view. "They object [to] the idea that they have to be somehow a little bit fair and balanced," Graham said. As for El-Sayed, he recently doubled down on his denial during a contentious exchange with NBC's Tom Llamas. "It's funny to me," El-Sayed responded. "I was born in 1984 down the street in Rochester Hills. I was raised here in Michigan, went to the University of Michigan, rebuilt the health department in this city, led the health department in this county — and you want to ask me about what's happening in Egypt in 1970? Are you serious?" "I get it, but you were asked a question, and you gave an answer," Llamas responded. "I have no ties, we have no ties," El-Sayed said, reiterating his denial. CBS CHIEF BARI WEISS' INVOLVEMENT IN VIRAL EL-SAYED REPORT SPARKS DEBATE AMONG CRITICS The Democratic hopeful told Llamas he hadn't had conversations with his mother about her alleged Muslim Brotherhood activity and accused the anchor of using "hearsay evidence from a tweet." "That's just not serious," El-Sayed said. "But you've also gone after the president for truthfulness and when people ask you a question, do you expect the truth?" Llamas then asked. "Are you insinuating that somehow I was lying?" El-Sayed fired back. "I don't know, that's why I'm asking," Llamas responded. "And I'm telling you that I was not," El-Sayed told him. Kennedy faced as a Catholic while running for president in 1960.

Under the new system, passengers can place orders through the Blinkit app while approaching a participating station and receive the items at designated delivery points on railway platforms or near station entrances during scheduled train halts.The service is expected to address a long-standing challenge faced by travellers who are unable to buy essential items during short stoppages. By integrating hyper-local quick-commerce logistics with railway operations, the initiative seeks to provide seamless access to critical products without disrupting passengers’ travel plans, according to railway officials.They said the partnership could serve as a model for similar collaborations across the country as Railways explores innovative public-private partnerships to improve passenger amenities and generate additional non-fare revenue.A senior railway official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told TOI, “This collaboration represents a major step towards modernising passenger services and station infrastructure. articles.title: Bus operators give dept 3-day ultimatum over double tax
articles.summary: Jaipur bus operators give transport dept 3-day ultimatum over alleged double tax on 24-hour permits, warning protests or strike after Diwali; seek refund, VLTD cap.
articles.body: Jaipur: Private bus operators have given the transport department three days to explain the alleged double taxation on 24-hour special permits, warning of protests and a possible strike after Diwali if the issue remains unresolved.Kailash Chandra Sharma, president of Private Bus Operators Association, Stage Carriage, Jaipur, said the department had allegedly been collecting double tax for two months despite repeated representations. Operators claim they are being charged for two days even though their permits are valid for 24 hours. They have demanded a refund or adjustment of the excess amount.Sharma said the association would approach the transport commissioner if the department failed to respond. Operators are avoiding a strike during Diwali, their peak business season, but may protest after the festival.He also flagged the high cost of vehicle location tracking devices (VLTDs), alleging that companies were quoting Rs 10,000-15,000 per vehicle despite a Rs 5,000 ceiling discussed at a transport ministry meeting in July 2026.Sharma urged the ministry to intervene, warning that operators would protest against companies if prices were not reduced. articles.title: Man & his teenaged son stabbed to death in Waluj; five of a family held
articles.summary: Father and teen son stabbed to death in Waluj MIDC after Navratra dispute; five neighbors from Haryana arrested as police probe motive and roles.
articles.body: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: A simmering dispute between two neighbouring families erupted into a double murder hours after Navaratra celebrations ended, leaving a 43-year-old truck driver and his teenage son dead and two others injured in Waluj MIDC in the early hours of Tuesday.Babasaheb Kirtikar (43) and his son Nihal (19) were allegedly stabbed to death at Krishnanagar in Ranjangaon Shenpunji around 1 am. Babasaheb’s two other sons, Sahil and Kunal, were also injured in the attack.Police have arrested five members of the Gaychand family: Rajendra Gaychand (53), his wife Shano (52), sons Nagesh (21) and Mayur (20), and daughter Mansi (19). Originally from Haryana, the Gaychand family lived next to the Kirtikars.According to the complaint filed by Sahil, the violence began near a Navaratra celebration venue at the Maruti temple. Sahil had gone to the venue when Rajendra and his son Nagesh allegedly confronted him and assaulted him with a wooden stick. When Babasaheb rushed to the spot along with Kunal and Nihal to intervene, the argument quickly spiralled into a violent clash.Citing the complaint, police said Mayur allegedly joined the assault. During the confrontation, Shano allegedly brought a large knife from the house and handed it to Nagesh. Nagesh then allegedly stabbed Nihal, leaving him critically injured. He allegedly turned the knife on Babasaheb moments later. At the same time, Mayur, Mansi and Shano allegedly attacked Kunal, police said.Babasaheb and Nihal collapsed on the spot with severe stab wounds and were bleeding profusely, the complaint stated. Residents took them to the Govt Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared both dead.Police believe the attack was rooted in an earlier quarrel between the two families. Sub-inspector Sagar Patil said the families had clashed a few days ago. At that time, Babasaheb was allegedly assaulted by members of the Gaychand family. Police suspect that hostility led to Tuesday’s deadly confrontation.Police commissioner Pravin Pawar said police teams moved swiftly after receiving information about the incident and arrested all five accused within hours. “The investigation is underway to establish the precise role of each accused and the circumstances that led to the killings,” Pawar said.Police have launched a detailed probe into the double murder and are recording statements from witnesses and family members.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: MLC poll: Rohit Pawar claims support of some Mahayuti neats for party candidate
articles.summary: Rohit Pawar says some Mahayuti leaders back NCP(SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil in Aurangabad Graduates MLC poll; demands higher drought aid.
articles.body: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar on Tuesday said that some leaders from the ruling Mahayuti have been supporting his party’s candidate for Aurangabad Graduates’ Constituency polls on Oct 23.Pratapsinh Patil of NCP (SP) is taking on Satish Chavan of NCP in Aurangabad Graduates’ Constituency poll.“There is a highly negative atmosphere against the opponent candidate. Even some of the ruling party leaders are supporting our candidate,” he told media persons in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Naming Abdul Sattar, Sillod Shiv Sena MLA who has openly supported Patil, Pawar said he expresses thankfulness towards Sattar for supporting a “good” candidate.Taking a jibe at Chavan, Pawar said the sitting MLC had tried his luck in the 2024 assembly poll, knowing that he would be on shaky ground during Aurangabad Graduates’ Constituency polls.“The voters will ensure his defeat. Neither money nor muscle power will work. Graduate voters are self-respecting and they will not bow before anybody,” Pawar said.The NCP (SP) MLA also accused Chavan of maintaining silence during the recent agitation of MPSC candidates and other pressing issues. “Voters say that he appears briefly for 15 days during poll campaigning and remains elusive for the next six years,” Pawar said.Pawar also demanded that the state govt release Rs1 lakh per hectare aid to farmers and Rs25,000 aid per family for farm labourers affected by the drought.“Amid waiting for substantial help, the state govt has announced the release of merely Rs5,000 to farmers. It is a mockery of the pain experienced by farmers,” he said.Pawar also said that Maharashtra would witness a change of power during the next elections. “The drought of 1972, followed by an emergency declared later, eventually saw a change of power in the country previously. The situation is similar now and we have an undeclared emergency in the country,” he said.On President Droupadi Murmu’s scheduled visit to Nashik on Oct 31 for the traditional flag-hoisting ceremony that marks Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela’s beginning, Pawar said the President should first “study” what is happening for preparations of the religious event.“There is large-scale corruption in the Kumbh Mela arrangements at Nashik. The President should consider why she was side-lined during the Ram Temple consecration ceremony at Ayodhya and also for inauguration of the new Parliament building,” he said.On the proposed Nagpur-Goa Shaktipeeth highway, Pawar said the ministry led by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari should take over the project from the state to save excess spending. “The road project is not needed in the first place. If the govt wants to push it, it should give farmers compensation equal to 10 times the existing market rates,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news.
